report_name: AI-Driven Cyberattacks Now Fully Operational, Flashpoint Reports

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Cybercriminals use AI to generate highly convincing, context-aware phishing and social engineering content, increasing the effectiveness and scale of initial access campaigns.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: AI is used to automate and accelerate target profiling and reconnaissance, compressing the time from target identification to exploitation.

attack_patterns.name: Polymorphic Code
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors leverage AI to create polymorphic malware and evasion scripts, which can better evade signature-based detection tools.

attack_patterns.name: Develop Capabilities
attack_patterns.description: AI assists cybercriminals in vulnerability research and exploit development, lowering the skill barrier required to create sophisticated attack tools.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The operationalization of AI by cybercriminals has contributed to a 45% surge in Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) activity, which involves encrypting victim data for extortion.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: The report highlights the theft of 1.7 billion credentials in the first half of 2026, a process that can be accelerated or enhanced by AI-driven tools for credential access.

attack_patterns.name: Generate Malicious Commands
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors use private, uncensored LLMs to generate malicious commands and scripts, bypassing the restrictions and safety guardrails of public AI models.

tools.name: Custom Large Language Models
tools.description: Custom, uncensored Large Language Models (LLMs) run on private infrastructure by cybercriminals to generate malicious content like phishing emails and malware code, without the safety guardrails of public models.

infrastructure.name: Private LLM Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Private infrastructure used by cybercriminals to run custom, uncensored Large Language Models (LLMs) for generating malicious content and avoiding detection by researchers.
